- A surprisingly HUGE amount of historical inaccuracies. Here are examples, for those who interested:


Uniforms/models:
- Russian with late war wool-padded jacket: the M43 Telogreika (Pre 1943-45) instead of M41 Telogreika (1941-43).
- There are Axis soldiers with Spanish's Blue Division decal appeared in most of the missions. By historical facts, they should never existed in this game at all.
- Strange and inaccurate uniforms for Afrika Korps and Western front Germans, also lack of variation.
- Greatcoat for some of Afrika Korps men, many can be used during night missions.
- Too well looking and inaccurate German winter uniforms. And a white helmet is also missing.
- For Western campaign, I'd suggest to separate regular Wehrmacht troops into 2 versions:
  1) Regular Heer with more acceptable uniforms, plus Camo Smock & Zeltbahn. No greatcoat appear.
  2) Volksgrenadiers - for Hill 400 missions and the last mission, mix up between regular uniforms and proper overcoats.
- M43 (1943) German tunic shouldn't appear in 1941 tutorial mission.
- Too many FAT Germans in this game. (I believe the diversity this game need are uniforms and faces variants).

- Extra Axis units:
  1) Panzer Lehr Panzergrenadiers: Camo helmet (majority) + Field grey Panzer jacket, mix with regular troops as an elite unit in the Battle for Caen missions.  
  2) Fallschirmjagers: As an elite unit, they should appear as a main enemy force in the Hill 400 defending mission (6th Fallschirmjager regiment, accompanied with elements of 272nd Volksgrenadier Div). And they can be appeared in the last mission also (as a part of German 1st Parachute Army, mixes with regular soldiers).
  3) ***Italian troops (including Italian dialogues) & weapons must be appeared in every Africa missions by mixing with Germans. And "Italian Paratroopers" are recommend for the first 2 El Alamein missions (Folgore Division).
  4) Teenagers of Waffen SS (12th SS Pz Div) can include in the revised Caen missions. SS insignia are optional, but SS Camo are recommend: Plane tree & Oak Leaf patterns on smock and helmet, Dot44 on tunic and trouser, and Italian M29 camo uniforms as optional choice.

- US Army rangers appear everywhere in Normandy. For my suggestion, wounded prisoners in the first Caen mission should be regular army soldiers.
- There should be a British officer with visor cap appear in Africa (only equip with revolver).
- Wrong Beret color for Capt.Price (should be Khakis + Rifle Brigade insignia).
- British 7th Armoured Div in Caen should have a proper insignia on their uniform (rifle brigade).


Vehicles:
- Higgins Boat in Pointe du Hoc mission MUST be replaced by British's LCA.
- Lack of variations on vehicles, especially for German tanks. They only got Panzer II and Tiger I in the game. Recommend tanks: Either Panzer III Ausf.G or Pz IV Ausf.F2/G for Stalingrad and Africa fronts. Panzer IV Ausf.H and Panther Ausf.A for 1944-45 missions.
- WAY TOO MANY Tiger I. Their appearance should be slightly fewer for 1944-45 missions, but few of them can appear in 1943 Africa missions. 
- 16th Panzer Division's insignia appear on Half-track in every missions. The division only appear in the northern part of Stalingrad, and they never participate in any other location in this game. My suggestion is making the corrected insignia, but easier choice is just REMOVE it or make it partially visible.

- Some Italian vehicles in Africa missions is an optional choice.
- The Tiger I that appeared in 'The Tiger' (St. Louet) and the one that was mentioned in the Brigade Box's loading scene (Amaye-sur-Seulles) should be a different tank. Since the mentioned one should be Michael Wittmann's tank, while the Tiger I that appeared in the game is probably not.

- It was UNLIKELY that the German got tanks (especially Tiger I) to assists their counter-attack at Pointe Du Hoc and Hill 400. And in Pointe Du Hoc mission, what's drove Rangers to fall back should be the German's artillery or mortar bombardment.


Weapons:
- Too many MP40 for regular German soldiers, Kar98k should be a truly common weapon.
- Some of German should be equipped with a captured PPSh-41 and SVT-40 (fewer) in Winter missions.
- Anachronistic weapons: MG42 in 1941 Moscow mission, Gew 43 (also scope ver) appeared in the 1942 - Pre 43, and Panzerschreck appeared in Pre 1943 missions. 
- It's unlikely that PPS-42 existed in Stalingrad (no official records), but quite acceptable.
- MG42 should be an uncommon weapon for 1942 missions.
- Lack of variations on weapons for both side, especially the Axis. What I could recommend is:
  Gewehr 41; replace G43 in 1942 ~ Pre 1943 missions
  MG34 and DP28; both portable and mounted version, highly recommended
  Walther P38; main pistol for German troops
  Panzerfaust; main German anti-tank rocket launcher in 1944-45 missions
  Panzerbüchse 39; good damage on light armored vehicles, recommend to replace the Panzerschreck in Africa, 1943
  PTRS-41; Anti-tank weapon for the Stalingrad city hall mission

While for Italians (mentioned above):

Others:

But it's impossible in reality, since the date is already December 17th, which mean Wehrmacht should had been driven off by Soviet Counter-attack (December 5th) before they could even reach Moscow. Call Of Duty 2 is developed by Infinity Ward and released in 2005.
It is the second major installment in the franchise, released two years after the first.

This second opus is faithful to its predecessor, and features three campaigns set during the Second World War.
The Soviets, the British and the Americans are playable in very different but equally apocalyptic settings.
Your war journey will be the most heroic and brutal yet.

During the Russian campaign, you'll take on the role of soldier Vasili Koslov of the 13th Red Army Rifle Division.
You'll have to defend glorious Soviet Russia against the relentless onslaught of the Wehrmacht.
In addition to the Russian cold, the Germans will face the formidable Soviet army, inexperienced and ill-equipped, but valiant and ruthless.
You'll take part in the merciless Battle of Stalingrad to liberate the country from the Germans by advancing eastwards.
Glory to the Motherland and Comrade Stalin!

In the British campaign, you'll play Sergeant John Davis of the 7th Armored Division.
You'll have to survive the terrible "Desert War",
fighting against the Afrikakorps troops of General Rommel.
In addition to the great Battle of El Alamein in Egypt, 
the "Desert Rats" will fight the Germans in Libya and even Tunisia.

Finally, in the American campaign, you'll be Corporal Bill Taylor of the 2nd Ranger Battalion.
After surviving the D-Day in Normandy,
you'll have to reconquer France, then push the Wehrmacht back to Germany,
scene of the appalling Battle of Hill 400... 

Taking on Nazi Germany's dreaded Wehrmacht is no easy task.
You'll need to complete a number of objectives in order to weaken the Third Reich.
For example, you will have to blow up tanks with explosive charges, 
exterminate waves of enemies with a sniper rifle or a machine gun, 
hold a siege while awaiting reinforcements, 
destroy fuel and ammunition depots, 
find strategic enemy documents, 
fight from a tank or the turret of an armoured vehicle, 
combat the Luftwaffe with a Flakvierling...

The campaigns are very well made, but leave a taste of unfinished business, as if each one lacked a grand finale.

COD2 marks the return of the charismatic Captain Price, who will be seen again in Modern Warfare.
A certain Miller is also on board, and will be seen again in World At War. 
The allies include a man named Weaver, like in Black Ops. 
There's even a fighter by the name of Pearson, as in COD WWII.
The soldiers West & Zampella are an obvious reference to the co-founders of Infinity Ward.

Weapons suffer from a much more pronounced recoil than in previous games, but this in no way detracts from the thrill of shooting, which is as exhilarating as ever.
A minor drawback, however, is that when you're being shot at, the character you're playing is systematically aiming too high in the air, making it difficult to shoot back.
COD2 features a wide range of period weapons. 
Several rifles can be used, some with scopes: Kar98k, Mosin Nagant, SVT40, Gewehr 43, Lee Enfield, Springfield, M1 Garand, BAR, M1A1, Bren...
You'll need to hold your breath when using Sniper Rifles to aim as accurately as possible, rather like Sniper Elite.
A number of secondary weapons are also included, making them ideal for indoor combat: PPSh-41, PPS-42, MP40, MP44, Thompson, Sten.

COD2 is more beautiful, spectacular and scripted than its predecessors.
The game's atmosphere is breathtaking, 
and brings to life the atrocity of the Second World War with panache.
The music is very typical of the period, but is sparse and emphasizes moments of bravery and victory.
The actor who voices the soldiers deserves an Oscar for his dedication to the role, and for his insane voice.

This second COD is full of small improvements: 
enemies can be seen on the compass, and a grenade indicator makes it easier to spot them.
Unfortunately, however, it is not possible to throw back enemy grenades, 
which would be very practical, given the Krauts' penchant for throwing them with surgical precision.
Allied soldiers, on the other hand, can return grenades to the sender.
If you're playing on Veteran difficulty, your patience will be sorely tested.
Some sequences are insanely difficult, beyond the point of absurdity, 
making COD2 one of the most difficult games in the franchise,
alongside World At War and COD MWII 2022.
Progress is slow, the Germans are numerous, they react quickly, aim well and are very tough on the battlefield.
The fact that you can't save manually further complicates the task, and the auto-regeneration of health just makes the game playable.

Call Of Duty 2 is an excellent war game, almost as good as its predecessor.
It is, however, less realistic and much more brutal and action-oriented than the first game.
Beware of its high difficulty, which may put off inexperienced players.

Don't buy this game off of steam, it's way too expensive (as a result of Activision being money-hungry thieves). For such an old game with a barren multiplayer, it isn't worth its steam price even on sale, however, I recommend COD 2 for its campaign wholeheartedly. It's a campaign you'll remember vividly after playing it, and that's with good reason. 

Call of Duty 2 offers what is probably the greatest COD campaign experience from a game-play perspective due to it being relatively free of the overreaching grasp of post Modern Warfare COD games (most of the time). Often, you've a few ways to approach objectives and in some of the games best moments, you're flooded with objectives which you can tackle in any order you like. The game is challenging but not to a point of frustration (on hardened, veteran may prove otherwise however) with simple but gratifying gun-play, and despite the fact that you're capable of being a one man army at times, it makes you feel as if you're part of an actual squad of soldiers. 

The three campaigns contrast each other really well, with the American campaign being the most epic/cinematic, the British campaign being the most action packed, and the Soviets finding themselves somewhere in the middle. These campaigns will take you through Normandy, Northern Africa and Russia during some of the wars most iconic battles (D-Day, Stalingrad, El Alamein etc.) with great success in terms of making you feel like you're a part of it all. While there is a lack of any real personal story, I feel like that's for the better here, as I had mentioned prior that this is a very game-play focused COD. The fact it's so game-play oriented in terms of its singleplayer campaign really does wonders for replayability as well, as the first thing I wanted to do when finishing the campaign was to go back in and ramp the difficulty all the way up. 

In terms of its mechanics and graphics, the game holds up decently well considering its age. The lack of a sprint seems peculiar now, however it helps to make you feel grounded in the game and playing without sprint only adds to the feeling of really being there in the game's oppressive battlefields. Like I mentioned prior, the shooting is simple but it works, not much to say about it. However when you get to regenerating health there may be some protest. I personally believe regenerating health to work well with this game, as the insane amount of damage you end up taking in combat and the hordes of enemies you face would lead to you needing god knows how many medkits. Yes, it somewhat pulls you out of an otherwise really grounded experience, but it's not a big deal. Graphics are fine, animations are fine, it's nothing terrible and I imagine that, for the time, this sorta stuff on the scale its being used would've made some computers choke up slightly.

Call of Duty 2 is one of the greatest WWII shooters to have ever existed and is a must play for any fans of first person shooters. It manages to avoid falling down many of the pits that modern COD games would fall down (although it's great to see Modern Warfare 2019 and Cold War actually don't suck) and it avoids being overly dated. It isn't a sort of game where you play it to look into the past and see how groundbreaking it was, it's a game which you can play and enjoy to its fullest right now. The 7-8 hours of fast paced and relentless action will keep you engaged the whole way through and leave you wanting more.

The differences from the first game are apparent right away to those who played it, although everyone should be able to notice the improved graphics. Gone are manual saves, in favor of mandatory checkpoints. Gone is the HP system, in favor of regenerating health, and while that's been criticized as making modern shooters too easy, I actually like it in this game. (Sprinting's gone too, for some reason, but it's not much of an issue.)

As good as the first game was, progression could get annoyingly difficult due to its traditional health system. Regenerating health means you can take glancing blows without having to play hyper-cautiously after you've been hit a couple of times, which lets you advance without the risk of being instantly killed. It also encourages you to take the fight to the enemy; you're weaker on higher difficulties though, so you can't exactly escape the sheer brutality of the conflict. That, plus the fact that you're usually fighting with your squad, generally encourages sensible tactics like taking cover and flanking.

There were a couple of times where the rest of my squad wouldn't advance with me for some reason, but it's not a huge issue. I also felt a bit of disconnect between the regenerating health mechanic, considering how many hits you can end up taking, and the fact that you meet wounded soldiers in a couple of missions. I suppose this could be explained by your character(s) getting lucky/being tough, and patching themselves up between levels.

A more noticeable issue is the fact that enemy soldiers endlessly spawn sometimes until you reach an objective. It's not game-ruining, but it made things frustrating occasionally, given that I'm the kind of player who prefers to take cover and advance slowly but carefully. As you can imagine, a tactical approach and infinitely spawning enemies don't mix terribly well. If I had to find a silver lining to this, I would say that it encourages aggressive play, but unlike the regenerating health it's kind of limiting with regards to how effective different tactics will be against it.


While the Russian campaign is a retread of Stalingrad from the first game, it was still enjoyable to play, especially without the ahistorical "one rifle for five men" from the first game's depiction. The British and American campaigns however are even better. Most of the British campaign is set in North Africa, which you don't see a lot in WWII shooters. It's a welcome setting and quite fun, even if the German Panzer IIs in the tank combat missions are rather inaccurately depicted as having impenetrable front armor and bigger guns than they ever actually had. Meanwhile, the American campaign starts by putting you in the middle of the D-Day landings, which weren't featured in the first Call of Duty. The missions get a little punishing near the end of the American campaign, but it's not as difficult as CoD 1 could be.

On a lighter note, the German voice clips in this game are more exaggerated than in CoD 1, which I view as neither a good or bad thing, just different. The historical cutscenes help establish context for the fighting and are a good addition, but they have odd Military Channel watermarks in the bottom right corner, which is apparently because [url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/09/23/military-channel-cod]Activision struck a deal with them to produce said cutscenes for the game[/url]. When I first saw them I admittedly thought they looked like cheap footage ripped from somewhere, but that seems to not be the case. The Military Channel itself has since been renamed to the "American Heroes Channel".


The multiplayer is more active than CoD 1's, which is good considering the scene for that game was a bit moribund, but it's not super popular either. Although most of the populated servers are modded, and there certainly are bots filling a number of them, it shouldn't be too hard to find a game with living humans in it. I'd attribute this to there being people who believe CoD 2's multiplayer is one of the finest in the series if not the finest, and to be honest it's certainly up there. There's no sprinting or vehicles like in CoD 1's United Offensive expansion, but hit markers make their first appearance, and of course there's regenerating health.

Be advised: on some systems you might need to do some tweaking to get the multiplayer client working, including, strangely enough, plugging a microphone into your computer irregardless of whether you actually use it. You may also need to deal with some lag if the populated servers at any particular moment are far away from you.

Here are some reasons to play Call of Duty 2:

It's a classic game that's perfect for some nostalgic fun. Remember the good old days when you could blow stuff up without any consequences? Yeah, me too.

The weapons are just plain awesome. From the trusty M1 Garand to the devastating Panzerschreck, you'll have a blast trying out all the different firearms.

The graphics may not be as fancy as some of the newer games, but that just adds to the charm. It's like playing a vintage action movie, complete with cheesy one-liners and over-the-top explosions.

The campaign mode is pretty epic, with a variety of different missions that will keep you on your toes. You'll storm the beaches of Normandy, fight through the deserts of North Africa, and even take part in the Battle of Stalingrad.

You'll feel like a total badass as you mow down hordes of enemies. Just remember to take cover every once in a while, or you'll end up as Swiss cheese.

So, there you have it. Call of Duty 2 may be an oldie, but it's definitely a goodie. Give it a shot and see for yourself why this game is still so popular after all these years.

Call of Duty 2 is sequel of successful first person shooter with very strong and top-notch presentation. You will experience through the perspectives of four soldiers in three campaigns which bring you to several memorable battle such as Stalingrad, Second Battle of El Alamein in Egypt, and Pointe du Hoc in D-Day. 

---------------------------------------------------------
Each campaign briefs you with short historical video before bring you right in the battlefield without any interrupted cutscene. Everything is built to create tension and deliver chaotic WWII atmosphere start to end. The scream of injured soldier, commander keeps yelling the order, German battle cry, dust, explosion, bullet tracers, particle effect, very detailed weapon and solid gunplay. They are just perfect.

Call of Duty 2 has linear campaign, but fills with non-linear path. Most of the time, you are free to approach any objective by your choice. Go straightforward or take alternative route to secure one by one and it emphasizes the variety of playthrough even in small area. Smoke grenade serve as tactical feature to disable enemy visual and push allied forces, but it’s limited per level. 

The game also introduces regenerate health to the series and set standard formula of full-scaled regenerated health system in modern video games. The purpose is to maintain the flow of combat and player's survival chances instead of reload save over and over. On higher difficulty, it still offers great challenge as one good shot can send you back to latest checkpoint.

---------------------------------------------------------
However, the game sometimes takes away the realism because of AI design. They are definitely challenged and aggressive AI, but in bad way. The enemies definitely know where you are no matter what position you switch. 

They don’t hesitate to charge you in open area or ignore my allies and run straight to just melee the player. They can spam bunch of grenades in one spot because enemies are designed to prioritize player in first place. Enemy’s vitality is sometimes unreasonable high as they still running after taking 2 rifle rounds in the chest. These elements break the realism and represent poor AI design that has always been an issue in COD campaign. Checkpoints are friendly and consistent, but it sometimes keeps you in bad spot due to script design.

The multiplayer is still active and it feels very original. No perk, no level progress, just pure skill based of your awareness and precision.

---------------------------------------------------------
Call of Duty 2 has some flaw designs that can be overlooked on lower difficulty. The game still delivers finest campaigns in COD series and very enjoyable historical based shooter. Highly recommend for any shooter fans.

Ah, Call of Duty 2. This is the first Call of Duty game I've ever played, back when I'd go to a cybercafé to play online games and games my home PC could simply not run. This was one of them. While I never made it past the tutorial back then, I did remember it fondly, if only because the tutorial had me throw potatoes as if they were grenades. Having finally played it to the end now, what can I say about Call of Duty 2?

Well, to start with, I'd say that this is when CoD started shaping up to the behemoth it now is. They must have retroactively heard my "complaint" about the unrealistic nature of being able to carry two weapons, plus a pistol and 10 grenades, because in this game, your weapons are limited to just two (you can carry a pistol, but you'd replace a larger weapon with it, unlike in the first game, where they were their own category), and while you can now carry both smoke and fragmentation grenades, you can only carry four of each. At least you get binoculars now without having to lose one of your weapons, so you lose some, you win some.

Anyway, going back to CoD actually becoming CoD, this game saw the introduction of regenerating health, so no more scouting the map for health packs, just go behind a wall for a couple of seconds, and off you go. It also removed manual saving of any nature, be it quick saving or a regular manual save, so it's checkpoint only now. Still, the gameplay feels very good, and the sound design is excellent, you truly feel as if you were on a battlefield with how loud the explosions and weapons sound.

Graphically, there's a noticeable improvement over its predecessor. Its age shows, obviously, but it's still nice to look at, and I'd say it's become somewhat "clearer" to read the environment and find enemies, something that was a problem in certain maps of the original. Level design is also improved in my opinion, and there's new environments to fight in; a good chunk of the campaign takes place in the African front, for example, but we also get to see the Eastern and Western fronts.

And speaking of the campaign, I haven't talked about it yet. Well, I gotta say, it's pretty good, even though by the end of it, I got a bit annoyed at the overabundance of "hold off until reinforcements arrive" missions. It does make for a cinematic experience, but the lack of quick saving can lead to annoying moments when you get killed before a checkpoint hits during these sections. Anyway, the singleplayer mode is divided in three campaigns (though you can play them as one continuous story). It begins with the Soviet chapter; basic training (potato throwing included) takes place in the first mission, and off to the war with you. Once you're done with the first chapter, you unlock the British campaign, but you can continue doing the Soviet missions, and the game will take you to the British campaign afterwards. This one begins in the African front, once you're done there, you start the American campaign, there's another British chapter, and finally, back to the Americans again.

Overall, I must say I enjoyed this game more than I did the first one or its expansion, so I can easily recommend it.

Pros:
There is no contrived plot. You’re just playing through epic battles from WWII.

It’s still rated T. It’s not super dark, or gritty. You don’t have a bunch of ugly dudes getting angry and swearing a bunch, and trying to make you cringe by performing particularly inhumane acts.

You get to play as the British and Russians, as well as Americans, and get to fight in different environments. Snowy bombed out Russian cities, vast African deserts, and French villages and countryside.

Each mission stands on its own, so if you want to come back to this game for a quick battle or two, you can easily jump into whichever mission you want to. There are no long, unskippable cutscenes that make replay a chore.

Cons:
The characters are not memorable at all (expect Price, with his mustache, and MacGregor, with his Scottish accent), and those that do stick around are one-dimensional. There is no character development.

But you’re not really here for a plot or story. You’re here to take part in epic WWII battles, and CoD2 does that spectacularly.

*Single player campaign only review*

One of innumerable 00s World War II shooters. This is possibly the best of the bunch.

The range of actions in Cod2 is small – it’s aim down sights, shoot, crouch, reload, wait while your health regenerates. Sometimes you throw a grenade or a smoke if you are feeling spicey. But these are all incredibly tight. The guns sound punchy and feel kinetic. There’s noise and dust kicked up as you fight. And before you have time to think you are in another situation.

The game takes place in three campaigns on three fronts. There are Russians in Russia, Brits in Africa and then France, and Americans in France. You crawl through pipes, march in with tanks, fight door-to-door in villages and everything in between. The changing locations & situations – attack, defence, ambush – give the constant variety needed to keep you engaged.

There are turret and vehicle sections. They’re fine. You don’t get much freedom of action in them but they are intense and cinematic.

Sometimes the limits of the game’s age show. Mission maps are miniscule, and if you pay too much attention you may notice you are almost double-backing on yourself implausibly. There is no wildlife and no locals – every single human being you see is a soldier for you or a German. But the missions are vastly better than most, because the flow through is so intuitive. You’re unlikely to get lost or confused or frustrated as you are guided through effectively.

The tone is also occasionally odd. You are having a boisterous, raucous adventure.  This involves shooting your enemies when they are down – otherwise they will try to kill you with their spare pistol. You also blow up a building full of trapped enemy soldiers in an early Russian mission, followed by rousing music. And then between missions you are given solemn quotes about how awful war is. Pick one, Infinity Ward!

I would not recommend playing on the hardest difficulty. CoD2 is most fun when there is not too much friction. This is because of the limitations of the game’s design. You are confined to real weapons and regenerating health, so they have to shower you with enemies and grenades and force heavy recoil on you when you get hit. Otherwise how else to increase the challenge? But the result slows the game right down, forcing you to hide in cover and regenerate endlessly.

Play on hardened or lower and you can enjoy the game in its best form – racing from location to location, carving through the Nazis like a harvester through a field of wheat.

Overall, CoD2 is a classic for a reason. As high art it's 6/10. As moment-to-moment gameplay, it's 10/10

Where to even start with this game? Well first, I should mention that I play the game to speedrun the campaign, so the best information I can give you is solely from the campaign portion. That being said, I have put in a lot of time on jump maps and multiplayer servers in the past and can say with 100% confidence that the game is worth it just for the small, yet active community that still exists on there. Going into the campaign, this is on par with the difficulty of World at War, which is possibly the hardest CoD campaign to avoid dying in. The gunplay and movement (like most CoD games released from 2003 - 2012) is among the best of the fps genre to date. I've always said this and will keep saying this: games whose engines are based off of the quake engine are just superior. Both strafe jumping and shooting feel so good working in tandem, it's indescribable the feeling you get when you begin to master these skills. The story is solid and pretty realistic for a WW2 shooter that came out in 2005. Honestly, I would recommend this to anyone who was a fan of the old school shooters, but if you consider a 5-6 hour campaign a bit too short it may not be worth the price of its normal 20$ tag. I would wait until an Activision sale happens, which luckily enough there is one at the time of me posting this :-).
